reconstruction.statement:
The following sufficient-condition theorem concerns the specified Newton-support series, with supporting results w7-1/n1 and w7-1/n2. It does not assert a theorem for arbitrary selecting series or for multiplier-ideal-selected spaces.

Let n≥1, let k_j≥1 be integers, and let X=(P¹)^n and L=⊠_jO(k_j). Let h be the product Fubini–Study metric. On T=(C*)^n, in the standard frame e, use r_j=log|z_j|² and φ₀(r)=Σ_jk_jlog(1+exp r_j). With dd^c=(i/(2π))∂∂̄, θ=c₁(L,h)=dd^cφ₀ is the closed Chern curvature. Let ω be any smooth ambient Hermitian form on X, possibly nonclosed; θ is not replaced by ω.

Assume K=X; w is smooth, real, and torus-invariant; F=φ₀+w has positive-definite real Hessian everywhere on R^n; and ν is a smooth strictly positive torus-invariant probability on X. If ω is torus-invariant, ν may be chosen as ω^n/∫_Xω^n regardless of whether ω is closed. For a non-invariant ω an independent invariant ν is permitted, but its normalized volume is not asserted to satisfy the sampling hypothesis.

Let P=∏_j[0,k_j], and let Q be a nonempty rational polytope compactly contained in int P, with aff Q=b+W for b∈Z^n and W a rational vector subspace. Put d=dim Q and Λ=W∩Z^n. Normalize relative volume dq_Λ so that a fundamental cell of Λ has volume 1; for d=0, Q={b} has volume 1. For every integer m≥1 specify exactly
  V_m=span{z^αe^m: α∈mQ∩Z^n}.
These are global sections, and for every global section s of L^m this selection is equivalent to the existence of a finite C_s such that
  |s/e^m|²≤C_s exp(mH_Q(r)) on T,  H_Q(r)=max_{q∈Q}q·r.

The precise target envelope is
  E_Q=(sup{v: v is a genuine global θ-psh function, v≢−∞, v+φ₀≤H_Q+C_v on T for some finite C_v, and v≤w quasi-everywhere on X})*,
using canonical upper representatives and quasi-everywhere meaning outside a pluripolar set. No equality with the multiplier-ideal envelope is asserted. The gradient map ∇F:R^n→int P is a smooth diffeomorphism; put r(q)=(∇F)^−1(q) and F*(q)=q·r(q)−F(r(q)). Then
  E_Q=G_Q−φ₀ on T,  G_Q(r)=max_{q∈Q}(q·r−F*(q)),
and E_Q has canonical value −∞ on X\T. It is a genuine global θ-psh function and satisfies E_Q≤w everywhere.

The weighted norm ||s||_m²=∫_X|s|_{h^m}²exp(−mw)dν is positive definite on V_m. Writing dν=a(r)dr dτ on T with Haar probability dτ, the monomials are orthogonal and
  A_m(α):=||z^αe^m||_m²=∫_{R^n}exp(α·r−mF(r))a(r)dr,
  ||Σ_αc_αz^αe^m||_m²=Σ_α|c_α|²A_m(α).
The basis z^αe^m/√A_m(α) is orthonormal. Equivalently, the weighted norm is the unweighted ν-norm for h_w=h exp(−w), whose local potential is F and whose curvature is the closed form θ+dd^cw. For all sufficiently large m and all selected α, uniformly,
  c m^−n/2 exp(mF*(α/m))≤A_m(α)≤exp(mF*(α/m))
for some c>0. The weighted Bernstein–Markov condition holds: for every ε>0 there is C_ε independent of m and s such that
  sup_X|s|_{h^m}exp(−mw/2)≤C_εexp(εm)||s||_m  for every m≥1 and s∈V_m.

The actual selected dimensions satisfy
  dim V_m=m^dvol_Λ(Q)+O(m^{d−1})  if d≥1,
and dim V_m=1 if d=0. Thus d is the intrinsic section-growth dimension, and the leading relative volume is positive. V_m is nonzero in every sufficiently large degree, although some small-degree spaces can be zero.

For B_m=Σ_j|s_{m,j}|_{h^m}², where {s_{m,j}} is an orthonormal basis, and U_m=m^−1log B_m with value −∞ at common zeros, one has on T, for all sufficiently large m,
  |U_m−E_Q|≤C(1+Σ_j|r_j|+log m)/m.
Consequently U_m→E_Q locally uniformly on T and in L^p(X,dvol_ω) for every 1≤p<∞, where dvol_ω=ω^n/n!. The extended pointwise lower bound liminf_{m→∞}U_m≥E_Q holds on all X; on T there is two-sided pointwise convergence, and on X\T both canonical functions are −∞ for sufficiently large m. Global uniform convergence across these poles is not asserted.

The finite Borel measures converge weak-* against every continuous test function on X:
  d!m^−d exp(−mw)B_mν→μ_Q=Ψ_*(d!dq_Λ dτ),
  Ψ:Q×(S¹)^n→T,  Ψ(q,τ)=exp(r(q)/2)τ.
Their exact masses are d!m^−d dim V_m and their limiting mass is d!vol_Λ(Q)>0. When d=0 the limit is Haar probability on one n-dimensional real torus. When d<n, normalization by n!m^−n instead gives the zero measure. The limit is independent of the particular smooth strictly positive invariant sampling probability ν, although the Hilbert norms depend on ν.

For the relation to an arbitrary ambient Hermitian form, let g_ω(u,v)=ω(u,Jv). If d≥1 put S_Q=Ψ(relint Q×(S¹)^n); the relative boundary of Q has zero dq_Λ measure. If d=0 put S_Q=Ψ({b}×(S¹)^n). The restriction of Ψ to these domains is a smooth embedding, and S_Q has real dimension n+d. With dvol_{ω,S_Q} the induced Riemannian volume, there is a unique smooth positive function J_ω such that
  Ψ*(dvol_{ω,S_Q})=J_ω(q,τ)dq_Λ dτ.
The measure μ_Q is concentrated on S_Q and satisfies the exact density relation
  dμ_Q=(d!/J_ω)dvol_{ω,S_Q} on S_Q.
No closedness of ω is needed. For d<n, this is a submanifold density, not a density with respect to ω^n: μ_Q is singular with respect to every smooth ambient volume and is supported on the compact shell Ψ(Q×(S¹)^n), of real codimension n−d.

The following closed-curvature conclusions also hold. Write G=G_Q. The restriction of F* to Q is uniformly strongly convex in the directions W. For every r∈R^n the maximizer q(r)∈Q in G(r)=max_{q∈Q}(q·r−F*(q)) is unique. The map r↦q(r) is globally Lipschitz and ∇G(r)=q(r). Hence G is C^{1,1} and its almost-everywhere real Hessian has rank at most d. Put T_Q=θ+dd^cE_Q, a closed positive current; on T it equals dd^cG. Its local bounded-psh powers on T are given by the corresponding Hessian minors. Its nonpluripolar powers agree with these local products on T and are their trivial extensions across the pluripolar boundary X\T, giving no mass there.

If d<n, then
  ⟨T_Q^{d+1}⟩=0 and ⟨T_Q^n⟩=0,
despite the positive mass of μ_Q. Moreover, ⟨T_Q^d⟩∧ω^{n−d}, with the conventional zeroth power 1 when d=0, is locally absolutely continuous with respect to ambient volume on T and gives zero mass to S_Q. In contrast μ_Q(S_Q)=d!vol_Λ(Q)>0. Thus μ_Q cannot equal this mixed measure for any smooth ambient Hermitian ω, closed or nonclosed.

If d=n, then G=F on r(int Q) and
  det D²G(r)=1_{∇F(r)∈Q}det D²F(r) almost everywhere.
In logarithmic-angular coordinates the normalization is
  (dd^cF)^n=n!det D²F(r)dr dτ.
The kernel limit is exactly the nonpluripolar closed-curvature measure
  μ_Q=⟨(θ+dd^cE_Q)^n⟩.
For any smooth ambient Hermitian form, writing dvol_ω=a_ω(r,τ)dr dτ on T, its density is
  dμ_Q=[n!1_{∇F(r)∈Q}det D²F(r)/a_ω(r,τ)]dvol_ω.
This is a nonpluripolar product, not an asserted ordinary wedge of divisorial currents, and ω need not be closed.

In particular, consider n=2, L=O(4,4), product Fubini–Study h, w=0, and
  Q={(2+t,2−t): −1/2≤t≤1/2}.
Here b=(2,2), W=R(1,−1), Λ=Z(1,−1), d=1, and dq_Λ=dt. The entire selected space is
  V_m=span{z_1^{2m+j}z_2^{2m−j}e^m: j∈Z, |j|≤m/2},
so dim V_m=2⌊m/2⌋+1 and the limiting mass is 1. One has
  F(r)=4log(1+exp r_1)+4log(1+exp r_2),
  r_1(t)=log((2+t)/(2−t)),  r_2(t)=−r_1(t),
and the limiting measure is
  μ_Q=∫_{−1/2}^{1/2} [Haar probability on {|z_1|²=(2+t)/(2−t), |z_2|²=(2−t)/(2+t)}]dt.
Its support is a compact three-dimensional real portion of |z_1z_2|=1, and it is singular with respect to every smooth volume on X. With
  c(p)=p log(p/4)+(4−p)log((4−p)/4),
one has F*(2+t,2−t)=2c(2+t), and on T
  E_Q(r)=max_{−1/2≤t≤1/2}[(2+t)r_1+(2−t)r_2−2c(2+t)]−φ₀(r).
Adjacent selected monomial ratios are z_1/z_2. If z_j=v_j/u_j, the associated rational map is [v_1u_2:u_1v_2]; it has indeterminacy at (0,0) and (∞,∞) and is not a global submersion on X.

This example permits a genuinely nonclosed sampling background. Let ω₀ be the sum of the two Fubini–Study forms, choose κ∈R\{0}, set f=κ|z_1|²/(1+|z_1|²), interpreted as its smooth global torus-invariant extension, and put ω=exp(f)ω₀. Then ω is a smooth positive Hermitian form and dω=exp(f)df∧ω₀ is nonzero wherever df is nonzero. The sampling probability ν=ω²/∫_Xω² satisfies all the hypotheses, θ=4ω₀ remains closed, and the same mass-one shell limit holds.

Every nonempty Q satisfying the hypotheses has positive relative volume and positive limiting mass; the singleton case has mass 1. The theorem does not cover empty eventual selection, affine lattice congruence obstructions, polytopes touching the boundary of P, failure of the strict convexity condition on F, non-invariant obstacles or sampling, or singular or nonpositive sampling densities. It makes no assertion for arbitrary compact K, arbitrary selecting series, or H⁰(X,L^m I(mφ)). Identifying an ideal-selected space with this exact Newton-support series would require an additional result and is not asserted here.
reconstruction.proof:
The conclusions of n1 and n2 are available by the declared support. Their hypotheses coincide exactly with the geometric, convexity, polytope, weight and sampling hypotheses in this note. Thus they establish, by actual global monomials and their exact Hilbert norms, all the repeated selection, envelope, dimension, Bernstein–Markov, function convergence and weak-* kernel convergence statements here. In particular the intrinsic dimension is the growth dimension of these V_m, not automatically n; small zero spaces do not affect the eventual limits. We prove the additional ambient, closed-current and example assertions below.

First observe that θ=Σ_j k_jπ_j*ω_FS is a smooth Kähler form on (P¹)^n: all k_j are positive. It is the closed Chern curvature of h. Neither its definition nor any section or envelope argument depends on ω. If ω is invariant, ω^n/∫ω^n is a smooth strictly positive invariant probability and therefore qualifies as ν in n2 even when dω≠0. For a general ω, one can instead choose, for example, invariant product Fubini–Study probability. There is no reason supplied here that the volume of a non-invariant ω fulfills the invariance hypothesis.

1. Smooth density on the intrinsic shell. In polar coordinates T is diffeomorphic to R^n×(S¹)^n. The radial map q↦r(q) is smooth, injective, and has differential (D²F(r(q)))^{-1}, which is injective on W. Radial and angular tangent vectors are independent. The inverse on the image is recovered by q=∇F(r). Thus Ψ restricted to relint Q×(S¹)^n is a smooth embedding of dimension d+n. The same argument gives the embedding of {b}×(S¹)^n when d=0. The relative boundary of a positive-dimensional polytope has zero relative Lebesgue measure, so n2's measure is concentrated on the stated S_Q, although its support includes the shell's boundary.

For any Hermitian ω, g_ω(u,v)=ω(u,Jv) is a smooth positive Riemannian metric. Its induced volume on the embedded S_Q pulls back to a smooth positive density on the parameter domain. The product dq_Λ dτ is itself a smooth positive density there, with the singleton counting convention when d=0. Their ratio is a unique smooth positive function J_ω. For any compactly supported continuous test function on S_Q, change of variables in the embedding gives
  ∫ f dμ_Q=d!∫ f∘Ψ dq_Λ dτ
             =∫_{S_Q} f(d!/J_ω)dvol_{ω,S_Q}.
This is the asserted exact density relation. It uses no closedness of ω. For d<n, n2's finite-dimensional shell strata have zero ambient volume, so this relation is genuinely a submanifold density, not a density relative to ω^n. Its real codimension is 2n−(n+d)=n−d.

2. Regularity of the restricted Legendre transform. On a compact neighborhood of Q, the positive matrix D²F* has a positive lower bound λ in the directions W. In particular
  (∇F*(q)−∇F*(p))·(q−p)≥λ|q−p|²,  p,q∈Q.
The restriction is uniformly strongly convex. For d=0 this statement in the zero-dimensional directions is vacuous. Strict convexity on Q implies that q·r−F*(q) has a unique maximizer q(r).

The first-order variational inequalities at q(r) and q(s) give
  (r−s)·(q(r)−q(s))≥(∇F*(q(r))−∇F*(q(s)))·(q(r)−q(s))
                             ≥λ|q(r)−q(s)|².
Thus |q(r)−q(s)|≤λ^{−1}|r−s|. Also the two maximizing inequalities imply
  q(r)·h≤G(r+h)−G(r)≤q(r+h)·h.
The difference from q(r)·h is bounded by λ^{−1}|h|². Hence G is differentiable with ∇G=q, and G is globally C^{1,1}. This includes the singleton case, where q(r)=b and G is affine.

Apply the listed Rademacher premise to the globally Lipschitz map q:R^n→R^n. Its almost-everywhere differential H=Dq is the weak Hessian D²G. It is symmetric and nonnegative, by convexity, and bounded. Since q(r)−b∈W everywhere, its differential takes values in W wherever it exists. Thus rank H≤d almost everywhere.

3. The local powers, with no unstated product-continuity theorem. On T, the global closed positive current T_Q=θ+dd^cE_Q is dd^cG, since θ=dd^cφ₀ there. G is locally bounded there. To identify its local bounded-psh powers explicitly, mollify G in the real r variables, obtaining G_ε. Its Hessian is the mollification of H, and G_ε is smooth convex. The Rademacher/mollification premise applies to f=q: H_ε converges to H almost everywhere and in every finite local L^p, with a common bound. Also G_ε→G locally uniformly.

The functions u_ε(z)=G_ε(log|z|²) are smooth psh on T. Their complex Hessian matrix is
  (i/(2π))Σ_{i,j}(H_ε)_{ij}(dz_i/z_i)∧(dbar z_j/bar z_j).
Expanding its pth wedge shows that its coefficients are the corresponding p×p minors of H_ε, with the usual wedge signs and dd^c constants. On each compact subset of T the z factors are smooth bounded factors. Polynomial expressions in the uniformly bounded H_ε converge in local L^1 to the same expressions in H. Let C_p be the resulting current with locally bounded coefficients.

We verify that C_p is precisely the local Bedford–Taylor power, rather than merely a formal Hessian expression. Let C_0=1. Inductively, uniform convergence of u_ε and L^1 convergence with bounded coefficients of their (p−1)st powers give
  u_ε(dd^cu_ε)^{p−1}→G C_{p−1}
locally as currents. For the smooth approximants,
  (dd^cu_ε)^p=dd^c[u_ε(dd^cu_ε)^{p−1}].
Passing to distributions proves C_p=dd^c(G C_{p−1}), exactly the recursive definition of the bounded-psh local power. This reconstructs the required convergence in this C^{1,1} situation. Consequently the local powers are given by the asserted Hessian minors. Since rank H≤d, C_p=0 whenever p>d.

Now check every hypothesis of the listed nonpluripolar-product premise. X is compact Kähler; θ is smooth Kähler as observed above; E_Q is a genuine θ-psh function, finite on T and not identically minus infinity by n1; A=X\T is a closed analytic union of coordinate divisors; E_Q=−∞ on A; and it is locally bounded on T. The premise therefore applies for every 1≤p≤n. It says exactly that the nonpluripolar powers are closed positive currents, agree on T with the local powers just computed, and are their trivial extensions across A, with no trace mass there for every smooth Hermitian form. No stronger extension theorem is being assumed.

If d<n, this yields ⟨T_Q^{d+1}⟩=0 and ⟨T_Q^n⟩=0. For d≥1, ⟨T_Q^d⟩∧ω^{n−d} has locally bounded coefficient density on T, hence is locally absolutely continuous relative to ambient volume. For d=0 the stated convention gives simply ω^n, with the same absolute-continuity conclusion. The smooth (n+d)-dimensional submanifold S_Q has zero 2n-dimensional ambient volume when d<n. Thus this mixed measure gives S_Q zero mass, whereas
  μ_Q(S_Q)=d!vol_Λ(Q)>0.
They cannot be equal for any smooth Hermitian ω, whether closed or nonclosed. The positive kernel mass and the vanishing nonpluripolar top mass consequently coexist without contradiction; they describe different intrinsic dimensions.

4. The full-dimensional closed-curvature measure. Suppose d=n. Then W=R^n, Λ=Z^n, and dq_Λ is ordinary Lebesgue measure. If ∇F(r)∈int Q, conjugate equality shows that this point is the maximizer and G(r)=F(r). Conversely, an interior maximizer has the stationarity equation r=∇F*(q), so ∇F(r)=q.
